reply.text:
All checks pass — `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` (28/28) are clean, and a live Playwright run against the running server confirmed the full flow: customer list loads, client-side validation blocks bad submissions before any network call, the submit button disables while pending, successful orders show `created` with the real numeric id and reset the form, and repeat submissions work.

What I built, following the existing `devices` module's contract/context/module pattern:
- `services/orders.contract.ts` — `OrderApi` interface (`customers`, `createOrder`) plus `OrderRejected`, an error class carrying field-level messages for 422s.
- `services/orders.http.ts` — the real `fetch`-based adapter (`GET /api/customers`, `POST /api/orders`, mapping 422 → `OrderRejected`).
- `services/orders.context.ts` — `useOrderApi()`, mirroring `useDeviceApi()`.
- `modules/orders/orders.validation.ts` — pure `validateDraft()` (customer required, quantity integer 1–1000, note ≤200 chars), unit-tested.
- `modules/orders/orders.queries.ts` — `useCustomers()` query and `useCreateOrder()` mutation.
- `modules/orders/OrderForm.tsx` + `orders.css` + `index.ts` — the form itself, with `data-testid`s exactly as specified (`order-form`, `error-customer`/`error-quantity`/`error-note`, `submit`, `created`).
- `main.tsx` — swapped the composition root from the fixture `Devices` wiring to `createHttpOrders()` + `OrderForm`.

The pre-existing `devices`/`reading` modules were left untouched (unused but harmless) since nothing in the task asked to remove them.
